files.why: Framework-free AuditEntry entity: actor, timestamp, target kind+id, action, and the set of field-level changes.
Pure change-set computation (diff before/after into a list of {field, from, to}) so 'what changed' is domain logic, not UI glue.
Server shape (snake_case, ISO dates) + zod schema for audit records; DTOs stay in data/.
Map audit DTO<->core AuditEntry, mirroring the billing/scheduling mapper convention.
recordAuditEntry() POSTs a new audit record — the write path every change flows through.
fetchAuditTrail(targetKind,targetId) / fetchAuditEntries so compliance can read the history.
MSW handlers + in-memory log for /api/audit, matching how billing/scheduling mock their APIs.
View state (load/loading) for the compliance trail, following the composable pattern.
Renders one entry: who, when, and the changed fields.
The compliance-facing view listing the change history.
Owns the /audit route(s); required slice entry, re-exported by index.ts.
The slice's only public surface: auditRoutes, AuditEntry type, recordAuditEntry, fetchAuditTrail, auditMockHandlers.

Add "audit" to the `slices` array (the documented 'add a slice, toolchain follows' hook) and allow the new cross-slice edges billing/scheduling -> @slices/audit; CODEOWNERS-protected, needs architecture review.
Regenerated (not hand-edited) from architecture.config.ts so the audit folder gets its layer import overrides; consistency test enforces it.
Regenerated allow-list including the audit slice and the new emit edges; else depcruise fails the new edges.
Composition root concatenates auditRoutes, like the other slices.
Compose auditMockHandlers into the MSW worker.
After voidCurrent (has before+after invoice), call @slices/audit recordAuditEntry — the canonical cross-slice pattern is composable->another slice's public alias.
After a successful reschedule (has before+after appointment), record the change via @slices/audit.

uncertain: Making 'audit' a new slice vs. keeping per-slice audit logic inside billing/scheduling. I chose a new slice because compliance is a distinct reason-to-change spanning both domains, and architecture.config.ts explicitly says 'add a slice name here and the whole toolchain follows' — but a reviewer could argue each slice should own its own audit emission and there be no shared audit domain.

Emission point: I put the recordAuditEntry calls in the two UI composables (matches the README's only documented cross-slice example: a composable importing @slices/<other>). The alternative is emitting inside each data/mutations.ts, but I'm unsure whether the depcruise allow-list permits a data/ layer to import another slice's index — the documented precedent is ui-level, so I avoided it.

Where the acting user ('who did it') comes from. There is currently NO auth/current-user/session concept anywhere in the codebase and httpTransport sends no identity. I'd likely inject the actor the same way `now`/`today` are injected from the composition root, but it could instead warrant a shared/lib actor accessor or an app/providers entry — genuinely unsure, and 'user'/'actor' being a domain-noun question for shared/ adds doubt.

Whether the generated config files (.oxlintrc.json, .dependency-cruiser.generated.json) should appear as 'modified' — they're script-emitted from architecture.config.ts, so in practice you edit the source of truth and regenerate; I listed them because CI checks them.
Whether a UI view/route is even in scope — the request says 'a record', which is the write side; the read/display side (AuditTrailView, route) is my inference that compliance needs to retrieve it.
questions: This is a frontend-only repo with a mock API. A client-side audit log is trivially bypassable and unreliable — shouldn't the authoritative 'who/when/what' record be produced server-side, with the frontend only displaying it? That would drastically change the file list (mostly a read-only view).
How is the acting user identified? There is no auth/session/current-user anywhere today. Where does identity come from, and can I add a way to source it?

What granularity of 'what changed' does compliance need — a field-level before/after diff, or just the action (e.g. 'voided', 'rescheduled')? Today only voidInvoice and rescheduleAppointment exist as mutations.
Is a compliance-facing UI (a route/view to browse the trail) in scope, or only the recording of entries?

Which changes count? Only the two existing mutations (void invoice, reschedule appointment), or every future create/update/delete on invoices and appointments — and does viewing/reading count as a 'change'?
Adding a slice touches architecture.config.ts and the generated configs, which are CODEOWNERS-protected and require architecture review. Is that approval path expected/available for this work?
Retention/immutability requirements? Compliance records usually must be append-only and retained for a defined period — does that constrain the storage/API design?
